## Actionable

### P3: Paged-search acceptance disagrees at the 200-result boundary
- Lenses: coherence
- Location: M2 work packages / Acceptance ledger
- Why it matters: A test corpus containing exactly 200 results can pass T05's stated “200+” requirement but fail A04's “>200” requirement. That creates a concrete disagreement over whether the work package has produced sufficient acceptance evidence.
- Suggested fix: Use one boundary everywhere, preferably “at least 201 results” if the intent is to prove traversal beyond 200.

## FYI

None.

killed_by_audit.title: M3 cannot fit the stated worker-attempt budget
killed_by_audit.why: refuted - The quoted budget sentence is immediately qualified in the same paragraph: it is a "Default milestone budget" and "A documented override is required before exceeding the budget," plus "Split at verified milestone boundaries rather than run the entire program in one thread" — i.e. M3's fifteen-task-pair load can legitimately be split across threads or run under a recorded override. The plan never asserts that M3 must complete inside twelve attempts, so there is no real contradiction; the document already supplies the governed escape path the finding says is needed. (T12 also bundles its independent security reviewer into the same task row, so the 2x-per-task attempt arithmetic is not even a fixed floor.) This is a sizing observation dressed as an inconsistency.

killed_by_audit.title: Required OAuth-soak and journey-time gates are absent from A17
killed_by_audit.why: refuted - The ledger is deliberately a one-line index and, by the document's consistent convention, never restates numeric thresholds: A13 likewise says only "frozen-fixture quality/resource thresholds" while the ≤250 MB / ≤512 MB / p95 ≤500 ms numbers live in the prose section. The soak's dimensions are in fact enumerated in T22's acceptance row ("exact public-client refresh/restart/expiry/reauthorization/revocation receipts") and its scope ("long-duration auth acceptance"), and journey timing appears in A17 ("platform-specific timing") and T23 ("exact native GUI/plugin/provider timing"). The section text is normative ("Require an 8+ day production authorization soak...", "Do not silently relabel a failed acceptance gate", "Every skipped required gate remains incomplete"), and the approved-exception path the finding says is missing exists explicitly ("a documented provider-approved equivalent"; "seek an explicit promise change before publication"). No gate can be closed without them, so the claimed omission is not real.

killed_by_audit.title: Schema-5 is named ambiguously as both current state and cutover
killed_by_audit.why: refuted - The document and repository both disambiguate. The plan states "Current durable schema is 5," and repository inspection confirms it (packages/engine/src/open_brain_engine/engine/local_schema.py: PHASE1_STATE_SCHEMA_VERSION = 5; CLAUDE.md: "Existing Brain state requires schema 5"; docs/schema-migrations.md: "older runtimes refuse schema 5"). Since 5 is already the current state, "cutover to schema 5" is not a coherent reading. Line 75 settles it further: "Migration proof must construct schema-5 fixtures through the existing replacement path" — schema-5 is unambiguously the pre-migration corpus being migrated away from, which is also how A03 reads ("Schema-5 durable-file migration inventory parity"). The claimed ambiguity is not real.
